en: Sutta Nipāta 2.9 Kiṁsīlasutta “What kind of virtue and what kind of conduct should one have?”
What deeds should a person cultivate so that,
being rightly established,
they may attain the supreme goal?
“One should be respectful toward elders and free from envy;
one should know the proper time for visiting one’s teachers.
Knowing the opportune moment, one should listen to a discourse on the Dhamma.”
One should listen attentively to well-spoken words.
From time to time, one should go into the presence of the teachers,
casting aside stubbornness and behaving with humility.
One should recollect and practice the goal, the Dhamma, self-restraint, and the holy life.
Delighting in the Dhamma, rejoicing in the Dhamma, one should live accordingly.
Established in the Dhamma and knowing the discernment of the Dhamma,
one should never utter words that corrupt the Dhamma; rather,
one should be guided by true and well-spoken words.
Hate, lamentation, and wailing, ill-will, deceit,
hypocrisy, greed, and conceit; aggression,
harshness, impurity, and infatuation—
Having abandoned them, one should wander free from intoxication, self-established.
One should understand the essence of well-spoken words,
and the essence of concentration within what has been heard.
Neither wisdom nor learning increases for that man who is reckless and negligent,
even though he delights in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Noble Ones.
“Supreme are you in speech, mind, and action;
established in peace, gentleness, and concentration,
you have attained the essence of learning and wisdom.”
The ninth discourse, *Kiṁsīlasutta*.
